title: Turkey at the World Cup
description: The 2002 semi-finalists and holders of a record you can never forget — how well do you know Turkey's World Cup history?

questions.q: Turkey finished third at the 2002 World Cup. What is their second World Cup appearance — the first was in 1954?
options: That was their second World Cup appearance — the first was in 1954
That was their third appearance — after 1954 and 1974
That was only their first appearance
questions.explain: Turkey's second World Cup was in 2002 — their first had been in 1954 (Switzerland), where they lost 7–2 to West Germany in a brutal play-off. The 48-year gap is a testament to the difficulty of European qualifying.

questions.q: Turkey scored the fastest goal in World Cup history in the 2002 third-place play-off against South Korea. How fast was it?
questions.explain: Hakan Şükür scored after just 11 seconds against South Korea in the 2002 third-place match — the fastest goal in World Cup history. Turkey won the match 3–2 to claim bronze.

questions.q: Who scored that fastest-ever World Cup goal for Turkey against South Korea in 2002?
questions.explain: Hakan Şükür — Turkey's all-time top scorer — scored after 11 seconds after kick-off. Turkey won the match 3–2 and finished third, still Turkey's best ever World Cup result.

questions.q: Turkey lost their 2002 World Cup semi-final to Brazil 1–0. Who scored the winning goal?
questions.explain: Ronaldo scored the only goal in the semi-final, sending Brazil to the final where they would beat Germany 2–0. Ronaldo finished the tournament with 8 goals, winning the Golden Boot.

questions.q: Turkey's goalkeeper Rüştü Reçber had an extraordinary 2002 World Cup. What notable honour did he receive?
questions.explain: Rüştü Reçber won the Golden Glove as the best goalkeeper at the 2002 World Cup, conceding only 3 goals in 6 matches. He was famous for wearing his distinctive blonde-streaked hair.

questions.q: Turkey qualified for the 2026 World Cup — their first since 2002. How many years is that between appearances?
questions.explain: Turkey last played at a World Cup in 2002 and qualified for 2026 — a 24-year wait. Despite strong players and consistent Euro qualification, they repeatedly fell short in World Cup qualifying.

questions.q: What is the official name of the Turkish national football team as recognised by FIFA?
questions.explain: FIFA officially recognises the team as 'Türkiye' — the Turkish spelling — following a request by the Turkish government in 2021 to use the native name rather than the English 'Turkey'.

questions.q: Which Turkish striker scored a famous winner for Turkey against Senegal in the 2002 quarter-final?
questions.explain: İlhan Mansız scored the golden goal winner in extra time as Turkey beat Senegal 1–0 to reach the semi-finals. It was a golden goal (sudden death extra time), still used in World Cups at that point.

questions.q: Turkey's current star is a creative attacking midfielder who plays in Germany's Bundesliga. Who is he?
questions.explain: Arda Güler burst onto the scene at Real Madrid and became a key figure for Turkey at Euro 2024 with a stunning goal against Georgia. He is seen as Turkey's brightest talent heading into 2026.

questions.q: Turkey reached the semi-finals of Euro 2008, held in Austria and Switzerland. Who knocked them out?
questions.explain: Germany beat Turkey 3–2 in a thrilling semi-final at Euro 2008. Turkey had scored multiple dramatic late winners throughout the tournament before finally being eliminated.
